text:
owen: Heads-up — onboarding Notch22b (int4) on g5-16x. Quant quality ok vs control, but we're seeing p99 spikes and 2 hard OOMs during a 10s burst of long generations.

diane: Can you drop the allocation trace? What was the request shape?

owen: Mostly long completions, average prompt+gen ~1800 tokens in the worst window. Alloc tail:```
[2026-03-21T09:12:03Z] gpu_mem: total free 5.8GB
[2026-03-21T09:12:03Z] kv_reserve: attempting reserve 1.6GB -> fail
[2026-03-21T09:12:03Z] prefetch: queued 48 batches, peak_inflight_tokens 14000
[2026-03-21T09:12:04Z] oom: killed worker pid 4321
```

sam: That's consistent with prefetch + large max_new_tokens = bad combination for int4 22B. Suggest immediate emergency canary defaults: max_new_tokens: 200, prefetch_window: 16, continuous_batcher.max_concurrent: 8.

lucy: Also our KV slot reservation heuristic assumes 20% headroom; with quantized kernels the working set is tighter. For this model reduce kv_slot_reserve_ratio to 0.07 and enable kv_lazy_evict=true so we evict only on demand. That should cut steady reserve overhead.

diane: We should also add a soft cap in Router: if request.max_new_tokens > 400 for notch22b-int4 rewrite to 200 and annotate trace with reason. Better than failing.

owen: I pushed a one-line canary config: `notch22b-int4: {max_new_tokens:200, prefetch_window:16, batch_limit:3, kv_slot_reserve_ratio:0.07}`. Rolling to 2 hosts first.

sam: Good. Add fallback route to `notch13b-v2` with aggressive latency preference. On allocation failure we should attempt routing to fallback instead of failing the request.

infra-bot: Alert created: `eng-ml.notch22b.int4.oom_rate > 0.005 over 10m` -> #eng-oncall, #eng-ml.

lucy: For verification run this synthetic driver that mixes shapes (short, medium, long) to stress KV and prefetch:```bash
LOREM="$(cat lorem.txt)"
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  if (( i % 5 == 0 )); then len=600; else len=60; fi
  curl -s -X POST $REDWOOD_URL/generate -d '{"model":"notch22b-int4","prompt":"'$LOREM'","max_new_tokens':"$len"}' &
done
wait
```

diane: Run that against the canary pool and collect p50/p95/p99, OOM count, and kv_eviction_rate. Post results.

owen: Test results after config change: 120 jobs completed, OOMs=0, p95 from 820ms -> 480ms, p99 1.9s -> 1.2s, kv_eviction_rate up a bit but that's expected. CPU on host spiked but acceptable.

sam: Nice drop. Follow-up if we still see tail: instrument continuous-batcher to track per-batch token counts and add soft-throttle: if inflight_tokens > 10k pause prefetch for 100ms. That can smooth spikes without reducing throughput much.

lucy: Also document in model-catalog: for quantized 20B+ models we recommend default max_new_tokens <= 256 and prefetch <= 32 on g5-class and similar. Add checklist items: canary small pool, enable fallback, run mixed-shape synthetic burst.

owen: I'll open the catalog PR and ops runbook update. Rolling config to remaining canary hosts. Thanks.

infra-bot: Deployment rollout: notch22b-int4 config -> 5 hosts (2 -> 5), no new alerts.
